newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Ethiopian sugar factory plans increased output.
newsitem.headline: Ethiopian sugar factory plans increased output.

text.p: Ethiopia's Metehara sugar factory plans to produce 110,000 tonnes of sugar in 1996/97 to offset a domestic shortfall resulting from flood damage.
Planned production for 1996/97 would exceed that of 1995/96 (Oct/Sept) by 10,000 tonnes, the state-owned factory said in a statement on Wednesday.
Metehara is the biggest of Ethiopia's three sugar plants and escaped damage after floods hit two other factories -- Wonji and Shoa -- earlier in the year.
Wonji and Shoa are unlikely to resume full production this year, agriculture ministry sources said.
Last month, Ethiopia launched a tender to buy 25,000 tonnes of whites from the world market for delivery at Assab and Djibouti.
Bids are scheduled to be opened in the presence of bidders or their representatives in Addis Ababa on October 25.
Independent industry estimates put Ethiopia's normal annual output from the three factories at around 220,000 tonnes -- enought to meet domestic demand and give a small surplus for export.
